source.title: EasyClassifier: Honest, Reproducible Machine-Learning Classification for Researchers Who Do Not Program

page_placements.theme: Randomized-label controls reveal evaluation dependence and leakage

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates classifiers on a random-label control and reports held-out balanced accuracy, but does not measure whether deep networks fit random labels or report training error.
record.gate_note: The random-label control reports held-out scores only; it does not report training error or establish whether any classifier fit the random training labels. Other results concern evaluation bias and KNN distances, not the claim. The random-label outcome is recorded under fits_no_version because chance-level test performance alone cannot establish V1.
record.test_reason: The random-label control evaluates classification-score estimation, not memorization. No training error, random-label fitting time, corruption sweep, or learning dynamics are reported. Chance-level validation performance alone cannot establish any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately conveys the authors' interpretation that the random-label control indicates no predictive signal. Clarify that 48.8% is the nested-CV estimate, while untouched-half performance is 47.9%. Their broader conclusion concerns reducing optimistic evaluation bias, not fitting random training labels.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates selected standard classifiers on a random-label control using a held-out split and balanced accuracy; it does not reproduce the original deep-network training-error experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: For the random-label control, mean balanced accuracies across three splits were 48.8% for the nested-CV final estimate, 47.9% on the untouched external half, 55.6% for the comparison winner, and 52.9% for the naive estimate; chance was 50%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On this random-label control, EasyClassifier's nested-CV estimate was near chance, while selecting and reporting the best comparison score produced a higher estimate.

record.problems: The random-label results do not state whether the selected classifier fit the training labels, do not identify the classifier in the control row, and provide no uncertainty estimate for these scores.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on random labels were reported. Other benchmark results concern score-estimation bias and KNN distances, outside the claim.

untested.parts: Whether standard deep networks fit completely random training labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters; no training errors or model-specific random-label results are reported.
Relative fitting time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels during training.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its own gate note. These results neither test nor rely on the random-label memorization finding.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard deep networks fit completely random training labels to zero or near-zero training error without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep from clean to fully randomized labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and data augmentation on fitting random labels and generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

relation.reason: It discusses chance-level prediction on random labels without measuring training-set fitting or testing any claim version.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates classification-score bias using a random-label negative control; it neither tests nor uses the random-label memorization finding.

source_check.notes: No V1–V6 verdict is warranted: training error, random-label fitting time, corruption sweeps and memorization dynamics are not reported. The authors' conclusion concerns evaluation bias and absence of predictive signal.
